clue.text: Range of company found by MP on a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a standard abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: A company is accompanied by a Member of Parliament aboard a vessel, perhaps on a fact-finding cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean scope or extent, as in the compass of a singer's voice, so it fits range.

clue.text: A yacht capsized in Old China

indicators.note: a capsized boat is overturned and jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailing boat turned over in the waters of ancient China.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Europeans, following Marco Polo, used this name for the land now called China.

clue.text: Striker appears satisfied about everything

indicators.note: about means the word for satisfied goes round the word for everything

parts.note: demands that are satisfied are met
everything is all

explanation.surface: A footballing striker seems content with his whole game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but it is a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden hammer, as used in croquet, is a tool for striking.

clue.text: Ida strips a rampant evergreen

indicators.note: rampant means running wild, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Ida takes her clothes off in a wild manner, like a hardy perennial.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy Asian houseplant with evergreen leaves, popular in Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Around morning she gets a feeling of guilt

indicators.note: Around means the word she is wrapped about the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

explanation.surface: A woman wakes in the early hours troubled by remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame is the painful emotion from knowing one has done wrong, close to guilt.

clue.text: Not quite a heavyweight vessel?

parts.note: in boxing one weight class, named after a type of warship, sits just below heavyweight

explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the boxing weight division named after this kind of ship, the one class lighter than heavyweight.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship smaller than a battleship is this vessel, whose name also labels the boxing class just under heavyweight.

clue.text: Accountant may be after this three-card trick

indicators.note: a trick deceives, so the letters of three-card are shuffled into a new word

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper chasing a card sharp's three-card trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-card trick is a con game, but 'trick' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A British professional accountant is qualified as a chartered accountant, so the answer comes before the word.

clue.text: Takes advantage, gaining three points on centre court

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word court

parts.note: S, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A tennis player exploits a lapse to win three points at Wimbledon's Centre Court.
explanation.walkthrough: Centre Court is Wimbledon's main tennis court; here 'centre' just takes the middle letter of court.
explanation.definitionFit: To use someone is to exploit them, taking advantage.

clue.text: Footholds on the mount

parts.note: mount suggests a mountain to climb, but it is a horse, and the footholds hang from the saddle

explanation.walkthrough: Footholds on a mount sounds like rock climbing; the mount is a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops hanging from a saddle hold a rider's feet when riding a horse.

clue.text: Determined to give poor Rose an instrument

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters of Rose are rearranged

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone is set on giving a struggling Rose a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges ROSE into RESO, which is then followed by LUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firmly decided, the same as determined.

clue.text: Bulb lit up, when switched

indicators.note: switched round means the letters of the two words are swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: A light bulb comes on once the switch is flicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' and 'switched' suggest electric lighting, but the bulb is a plant's.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring flower grows from an underground storage organ, so it can be called a bulb.

clue.text: I made case out for specialised schools

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone argues the case in favour of specialist schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Academies are schools, often devoted to one discipline such as music or the military.

clue.text: The constitution should be all the better for them

definitions.text: The constitution should be all the better for them

parts.words: The constitution should be all the better for them
parts.note: a constitution, like the US one, is improved by formal changes to its text; read as health, a constitution is a bodily state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitution' can suggest one's physical health, improved by tonics, but here it is a nation's founding law.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal revisions to a legal document are meant to improve it, as with the US Bill of Rights.

clue.text: A student is after an alternative exam

indicators.note: the A and the student come after the alternative in the answer

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pupil chooses to sit a different exam instead.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a learner or student comes from the L-plates worn by British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a language exam, is an oral.

clue.text: Container to list in aircraft manoeuvre

parts.note: a barrel is a container, as for beer
a ship that lists leans to one side, which is to roll

explanation.surface: A crate is to be listed in the inventory of a plane's stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerobatic move in which the plane spirals along its line of flight.

clue.text: It may have a good nap on the flight

definitions.text: It may have a good nap on the flight

parts.words: It may have a good nap on the flight
parts.note: nap is the raised pile of a fabric and a flight is a set of steps, not a sleep on a plane

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a passenger sleeping on a plane; nap is the pile of a carpet and the flight is of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner laid on steps has a pile, or nap, and covers a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Sort out that messy collection of stones

indicators.note: sorting out reorders things, so the letters of the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tidy a jumbled jewellery collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple quartz gems are precious stones, and the plural makes a collection.

clue.text: Precise bill supported by a junior minister

indicators.note: in a down clue the bill sits above, held up by, the minister

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest, a junior church minister

explanation.surface: A precise piece of legislation is backed by a junior government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' suggests government; it is a church minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means exact, free from error, which is precise.

clue.text: It's a blow that has to be faced

definitions.text: It's a blow that has to be faced

parts.words: It's a blow that has to be faced
parts.note: a blow seems a setback to confront, but it is wind blowing against one

explanation.walkthrough: 'A blow that has to be faced' sounds like misfortune; the blow is a wind coming straight at you.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing directly against the direction of travel is one met front on.

clue.text: Person with two hips?

parts.note: the cry 'hip, hip, hooray' has two hips, and one who leads the crowd in it is the person meant

explanation.walkthrough: Everyone has two hips; the hips here are the shouts of 'hip, hip, hooray' led by a crowd's rousing leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads supporters in chanting at games starts the 'hip, hip' cheer.

clue.text: Girl came in to study the weapon

indicators.note: came in to means the girl's name goes inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman entered the study to look at a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A large mounted gun firing heavy shot is this weapon.

clue.text: Want to disguise hatred

indicators.note: disguising something changes its look, so the letters of hatred are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to hide their hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb meaning wish; it is a noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means a lack or scarcity, which is a dearth.

clue.text: Some harbour dues with which Indians are conversant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Port charges are something Indian traders know all about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversant' suggests familiarity with harbour dues, but here it means able to converse in a language.
explanation.definitionFit: A language spoken across northern India and Pakistan is one Indians can converse in.

clue.text: Break away from the craft

parts.note: a break is time off, and the craft is a ship, so this is sailors' leave ashore

explanation.walkthrough: 'Break away' suggests escaping or splitting off, and 'craft' a trade; it is a sailor's time off ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors given time off the ship to go ashore are granted this kind of break.

clue.text: A follower of Ethiopian emperor and a Russian emperor uplifted

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tsar was an emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: Two emperors, one from Ethiopia and one from Russia, are linked by a devotee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' reverses A TSAR into RASTA. Rastafarians revere Haile Selassie, emperor of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian, follower of a movement venerating Ethiopia's Emperor Haile Selassie, is called a Rasta for short.

clue.text: Heads up to deliver a knock-out blow

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word for heads is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: A boxer is told to keep his head up before landing the decisive punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NUTS into STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock someone senseless, as a knockout punch does.

clue.text: Exacting examinations, involving litmus papers?

definitions.meaning: severe trials that prove whether something is genuine
litmus paper is used to test whether a liquid is acidic

explanation.surface: Tough exams might include chemistry questions about litmus paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Decisive trials of worth are named after the old nitric acid test for gold, and litmus checks for acids.

clue.text: One has to be what one is

definitions.text: One has to be what one is

parts.words: One has to be what one is
parts.note: read literally, a person who has a thing is its possessor

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a philosophical truism about being oneself; in fact one who has a thing is its holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who possesses something is defined by having it.

clue.text: Sending out terminations

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of Sending are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dismissal letters are posted to staff whose jobs are ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusions or finishes of things are terminations.

clue.text: Getting fed up about midday?

parts.note: fed up seems to mean bored, but it is being fed around noon, at the midday meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like boredom or annoyance; here it is literally being fed, at the middle of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eating the midday meal is away from their desk, being fed around noon.
